def: The assumptions a model makes before seeing data, which decide what it finds easy to learn.
A tabular neural network that embeds each column as a token and applies a transformer over the column tokens.
Mapping a numeric column through periodic functions or bins before a network so that it can represent sharp changes in that column.
Replacing each column's values by their rank, rescaled to a uniform or normal shape, to tame skew and outliers.
A large model pre-trained once on many (often synthetic) tables that predicts on a new table without being trained on it.
A transformer pre-trained on synthetic tables that classifies or regresses a new small table in one forward pass by in-context learning.
Making predictions from labelled examples supplied in the model's input, with no change to its weights.
A maintained public benchmark and leaderboard for machine learning on small and medium tabular datasets.
